text:
ops-bot: Incident detected: elevated 5xx rate in nz-south1 ingress-gateway pool (threshold 1% -> 7%). Auto-page oncall.

mariA (oncall): I'm taking this — seeing spike in 502/504s from ingress in nz-south1, started ~04:05 NZT. Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/6128641234 and kpi: https://dash.redwood.internal/regions/nz-south1

kevin (sre): Confirming. Metrics: 502s primarily from connection reset upstream, increased latency in egress to mlworkers. Trying a quick query: `sum(rate(ingress_gateway_5xx[5m])) by (pool)` shows nz-south1 ~6.8%

jonah (runtime): Logs show lots of `upstream reset` from edgeproxy -> inference-gateway. Possibly conntrack exhaustion on nat instances. Example snippet:

```
2026-03-15T04:07:12Z [edgeproxy] upstream_reset id=abc123 remote=10.12.45.9:42934 cause=RST_STREAM
2026-03-15T04:07:14Z [edgeproxy] upstream_reset id=abc124 remote=10.12.46.2:42934 cause=conntrack_full
```

maria (oncall): Good catch. If conntrack saturation then traffic should be reroutable. What's immediate blast radius? Any customers on dedicated pools in nz-south1?

liz (support): I pulled recent support tickets — 2 customers on dedicated pools report failures in last 10m. We should call out customer impact if we start cross-region failover.

jonah (runtime): Quick triage plan: 1) drain edgepool-nz-south1 to stop new sessions 2) shift egress of new requests to au-syd1/au-north fallback 3) increase nat conntrack on affected hosts 4) investigate kv-cache thrash causing heavy egress.

kevin (sre): Agreed. Initiating pool drain. Maria, can you approve a controlled drain and reroute? I'll monitor connections.

maria (oncall): Approve. Execute drain and announce to customers. Keep canary at 5% traffic to confirm fallback.

jonah (runtime): Running drain command on edgepool controller:

```
# drain edgepool-nz-south1 (graceful)
kubectl -n edgectl patch edgepool edgepool-nz-south1 -p '{"spec":{"drain":true}}'
edgectl wait --pool edgepool-nz-south1 --drained --timeout 300
```

ops-bot: edgepool edgepool-nz-south1 drain requested by jonah. Job id: J-612864-01.

kevin (sre): Starting canary shift (5%) via routing policy change. Command: `routectl set-weight region=nz-south1 weight=5 --targets au-syd1=45,au-north=50`

maria (oncall): I'll post customer comms — short notice: we are routing traffic to fallback regions due to elevated errors. Liz, please prep proactive messages for the two affected customers (include timeframe and mitigation).

liz (support): On it, drafting now. ETA 6m.

tila (backfill): Observability: I see spike in conntrack close_waits across nat-1..nat-4 in nz-south1. sysctl shows net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count near limit. Suggest bump to 1.5x and roll hosts.

jonah (runtime): Bumping sysctl on nat hosts now (one-shot):

```
for host in nat-1 nat-2 nat-3 nat-4; do ssh $host "sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144"; done
```

kevin (sre): Doing gradual host reboot/replace for ones with the highest nf_conntrack_count. Marking two hosts for immediate replacement.

ops-bot: route change applied — nz-south1 weight set to 5%. au-syd1=45%, au-north=50%.

maria (oncall): Monitoring 1m. If 5xx stays >2% we escalate to full 100% shift.

sam (rd): Noting that some model variants are heavier on kv lookups; we saw model-x-13b producing more egress calls. If we redirect only some model traffic we can reduce pressure. Can we route model-x to au-north only?

jonah (runtime): Yes, per-model routing available. Implementing temporary routing rule to pin model-x to au-north: `routectl pin model=model-x region=au-north`

kevin (sre): After drain, connection reset errors dropped ~60% from logs but 502s persist at ~2.2% system-wide. NZ-specific 5xx now ~1.6%. Still above baseline but trending down.

maria (oncall): Good. Liz — customer comms ready?

liz (support): Sent to both customers: short blurb + link to status page. Also created ticket CS-612864 for follow-up.

eng-lead-anne: Thanks for fast mitigation. How long before we can hand to day SRE?

maria (oncall): I'll continue monitoring for 30m. If metrics stay steady and conntrack hosts replaced, I'll hand off. Preparing handoff note.

maria (oncall): Handoff note: "Mitigations: drained edgepool-nz-south1, routing weights adjusted to au-syd1/au-north, conntrack bump + host replacements started, model-x pinned to au-north. Customer notifications issued. Current nz-south1 5xx=1.3% (down from 6.8%). Keeping 5% canary to validate recovery. Oncall -> maria (until 04:40NZT)."

pagerduty-bot: Pager Duty: Incident 612864 acknowledged by maria. Escalation paused.

tila (backfill): Replacements finished for nat-2 and nat-3. nf_conntrack_count dropped to 35% capacity. No obvious kernel panics.

kevin (sre): Removing drain at 04:22NZT to bring pool back up with controlled concurrency: `edgectl wait --pool edgepool-nz-south1 --ready` then `kubectl patch` to set drain=false

ops-bot: edgepool edgepool-nz-south1 marked ready.

jonah (runtime): Rolling traffic back: set weight nz-south1=30 au-syd1=35 au-north=35, monitor for 10m.

maria (oncall): Monitoring. If 5xx creeps >1% we'll revert.

kevin (sre): 10m mark: nz-south1 5xx=0.6% (within normal). No customer escalations from support.

liz (support): Customers acknowledged and closing initial tickets. Will follow up with RCA requests.

sam (rd): Action item: add conntrack autoscaling play to runbook and add an anomaly alert for model-driven egress spikes (model-x pattern).

eng-lead-anne: Assigning follow-up to jonah/kevin/sam for post-incident. Please include timeline, root cause hypothesis (conntrack + model-driven egress + kv-cache pressure), and mitigation plan.

maria (oncall): Closing incident channel at 04:40NZT. Final note: brief outage window ~04:05-04:22NZT, partial impact to two customers, mitigated without full region failover. Will file P0 follow-up.

ops-bot: Incident 612864 status: resolved (mitigations applied). Postmortem owner assigned: jonah.

maria (oncall): Thanks team.

kevin (sre): +1 — thanks all.

sam (rd): Adding eval tests to prevent model-x causing sudden egress spikes in future.

maria (oncall): End thread.
